name: HCG + SERM restart

lead: An HPTA restart is the attempt to get the hypothalamic-pituitary-testicular axis, the body's own testosterone signalling chain, working again after testosterone, anabolics or SARMs have suppressed it. The combination uses hCG, which stimulates the testes directly, and a SERM, which acts at the brain to raise LH and FSH.

The appearance link is retention of muscle, a leaner body, skin and libido that depend on natural androgen levels. Forum members post blood-test updates showing recoveries and also cases where restart failed and they stayed on TRT.

paras: Forum threads describe a sequence in which hCG is used first for a period, followed by a SERM such as clomiphene or tamoxifen (Nolvadex) for several weeks, with blood tests before and after. Users discuss which SERM they tolerated better, and many ask for a doctor who is informed about it. Specific amounts and sourcing are not covered here.

All components are prescription medicines in the US and UK. Clomifene side effects include visual symptoms, headaches and hot flushes, and the drug is banned in sport by WADA. hCG in men can raise androgen production, with cautions in some health conditions and for adolescents. Users in threads report that restarts do not always work.

angle.text: Users attempt the restart to keep the physique benefits of normal testosterone after stopping TRT or a cycle. Results reported in forum threads vary, from full recoveries to returning to TRT.

lead: HCG + SERM restart, often called an HPTA restart, is a protocol discussed by anabolic and TRT users to recover natural testosterone production after suppression by exogenous hormones, SARMs or other drugs.[1][2]

Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) mimics luteinizing hormone and stimulates the Leydig cells of the testes to make testosterone, and is used medically in some forms of male hypogonadism and to maintain testicular function and fertility.[3] A SERM such as clomifene works in the hypothalamus, blocking estradiol's negative feedback and raising GnRH, LH and FSH; it is sometimes used off-label in men as an alternative to testosterone replacement.[4]

People care about this for appearance reasons: muscle mass, body fat, libido and general vitality are linked to androgen levels, and a successful restart is how some users hope to come off TRT or end a cycle without losing gains.
infobox: hCG plus a SERM (clomiphene or tamoxifen)

paras: Forum members describe the restart as a way to recover after prolonged TRT or after SARM and finasteride use, and one widely read thread documents a user whose androgen levels rebounded to high values after restart.[5] Other users reaching the end of two years on TRT say they accept that it may be lifelong but want to test whether they can function naturally; if the restart fails, they return to TRT.[6]

hCG stimulates Leydig cells to make testosterone, and intratesticular testosterone supports sperm production. It is used alone or with testosterone in certain hypogonadism cases and to prevent testicular atrophy.[3] Clomifene blocks estradiol feedback and raises LH and FSH; enclomifene is its pro-androgenic isomer.[4]

On T Nation, HPTA restart threads are linked from general TRT discussions and users advise that an informed doctor helps.[1] Members compare Clomid with Nolvadex, with one reporting four weeks of Nolvadex and calling hCG followed by a SERM a fairly standard restart.[7] Another thread, started by a user changing from Nolvadex to Clomid, shows someone planning hCG then a SERM after two years on TRT.[8] Some users debate whether SERMs are preferable to aromatase inhibitors for restarts.[9] One user reports mixed results on hormone numbers on hCG alone.[10]

Clomifene's listed adverse effects include visual symptoms, headaches and hot flushes, with rare liver effects; it is prescription-only in the US and UK and appears on the WADA prohibited list.[4] hCG labelling in men cautions for prolonged androgen increase, heart failure, hypertension, migraine and epilepsy, and for adolescents because of growth-plate and early-development risk.[3]
No studies found on the combined community protocol. Clinical literature exists for the individual drugs in male hypogonadism, as summarised in the encyclopedia references.[3][4]

lore.intro: HPTA restart threads on T Nation mix personal logs with questions about which SERM and what lab results to expect.[8][2][3]
